LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_: Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets and let pW and qW be the output laws. If a single reverse channel R recovers the original output–input joint law for both p and q, then D(pW‖qW) = D(p‖q), including when the divergences are infinite.

For finite discrete alphabets with supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), a channel W preserves D(p‖q) exactly when one reverse channel R reproduces each original joint law of (Y,X) by sampling Y from its output law and drawing X through R, for both input laws p and q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_chan: Let W be a channel between finite discrete alphabets with supp(p) ⊆ supp(q). The real-valued divergences before and after W are equal if and only if a single reverse channel reconstructs the full output–input law under both p and q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_map_eq_iff_: For finite discrete alphabets and supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), a statistic T preserves D(p‖q) exactly when one channel R from statistic values to observations recovers the joint law of (T(X),X) for each of the two input laws.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_map_: For finite discrete alphabets with supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), the real-valued divergence between the laws of T(X) under p and q equals D(p‖q) exactly when a single channel from T(X) back to X reproduces both original joint laws of (T(X),X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_eq_of_isSuf: A sufficient channel W between finite discrete alphabets preserves the KL divergence between every ordered pair of model laws: D(PₛW‖PₜW) = D(Pₛ‖Pₜ), also when the divergence is infinite.
A sufficient statistic T between finite discrete alphabets preserves the KL divergence between every ordered pair of model laws, including divergence equal to infinity.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientChann: Consider two laws P₀ and P₁ on a finite discrete alphabet, with supp(P₀) ⊆ supp(P₁). A channel W with finite discrete output is sufficient for this two-law family exactly when D(P₀W‖P₁W) = D(P₀‖P₁).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientStati: Consider two finite discrete model laws with supp(P₀) ⊆ supp(P₁). A finite-valued statistic T is sufficient for this two-law family exactly when the divergence between its output laws under P₀ and P₁ equals D(P₀‖P₁).
